job.name: Job
job.note: The afflicted just man of Hus, answering his friends and pleading his cause before God.

1.t: Behold my eye hath seen all these things, and my ear hath heard them, and I have understood them all.

2.t: According to your knowledge I also know: neither am I inferior to you.

3.t: But yet I will speak to the Almighty, and I desire to reason with God.

4.t: Having first shewn that you are forgers of lies, and maintainers of perverse opinions.

5.t: And I wish you would hold your peace, that you might be thought to be wise men.

6.t: Hear ye therefore my reproof, and attend to the judgment of my lips.

7.t: Hath God any need of your lie, that you should speak deceitfully for him?

8.t: Do you accept this person, and do you endeavour to judge for God?

9.t: Or shall it please him, from whom nothing can be concealed? or shall he be deceived as a man, with your deceitful dealings?

10.t: He shall reprove you, because in secret you accept his person.

11.t: As soon as he shall move himself, he shall trouble you: and his dread shall fall upon you.

12.t: Your remembrance shall be compared to ashes, and your necks shall be brought to clay.

13.t: Hold your peace a little while, that I may speak whatsoever my mind shall suggest to me.

14.t: Why do I tear my flesh with my teeth, and carry my soul in my hands?

15.t: Although he should kill me, I will trust in him: but yet I will reprove my ways in his sight.

16.t: And he shall be my saviour: for no hypocrite shall come before his presence.

17.t: Hear ye my speech, and receive with your ears hidden truths.

18.t: If I shall be judged, I know that I shall be found just.

19.t: Who is he that will plead against me? let him come: why am I consumed holding my peace?

20.t: Two things only do not to me, and then from thy face I shall not be hid:

21.t: Withdraw thy hand far from me, and let not thy dread terrify me.

22.t: Call me, and I will answer thee: or else I will speak, and do thou answer me.

23.t: How many are my iniquities and sins? make me know my crimes and offenses.

24.t: Why hidest thou thy face, and thinkest me thy enemy?

25.t: Against a leaf, that is carried away with the wind, thou shewest thy power, and thou pursuest a dry straw.

26.t: For thou writest bitter things against me, and wilt consume me for the sins of my youth.

27.t: Thou hast put my feet in the stocks, and hast observed all my paths, and hast considered the steps of my feet:

28.t: Who am to be consumed as rottenness, and as a garment that is motheaten.
